title: Simon the sorcerer tries to buy power — Acts 8
paragraphs: Simon the sorcerer tries to buy power — Acts 8

He wanted the fire of God
without the God of fire.

Simon saw hands laid on people.
He saw the Spirit move.
He saw power fall.
And he reached for his wallet.
That is the scandal of Acts 8.

Not just a sorcerer in Samaria.
A man exposed.
A heart that wanted influence more than surrender, wonder more than holiness, platform more than repentance.

He believed enough to stay close.
But not enough to die to himself.

So when Simon told the apostles, “Give me this power also,” Peter did not pat him on the back. He cut straight to the cancer: “May your silver perish with you… your heart is not right before God.” (Acts 8:20–21)
Strong words.

Because sacred things cannot be bought.
The Holy Spirit is not merchandise.
Anointing is not for sale.
The kingdom of God does not bow to ambition dressed in religious language.
And here’s what we miss—

Simon is not just a villain from the first century.
He is a mirror.

Every time we want the spotlight without the cross.
Every time we crave gifting without godliness.
Every time we ask for ministry influence while secretly feeding pride.
We are standing too close to Simon.
But grace walks in where pride gets exposed.

Peter did not only rebuke him. He told him to repent.
That means the door was still open.
Mercy was still calling.
Even for a man who tried to purchase what only heaven can give.
That is the Gospel.

You cannot buy salvation.
You cannot earn the Spirit.
You cannot manipulate grace.
But what you could never purchase, Jesus gives freely to the repentant sinner.

At the cross, God did not offer a transaction.
He offered a rescue.

So come empty-handed.
Come honest.
Come broken.
The blood of Jesus is enough for the proud heart, the greedy heart, the performative heart, the heart that wanted ministry for self instead of Christ.

Repent.
Believe.
Receive what money never could.
